stem: Each iteration of a variational algorithm sets its parameters from the previous Estimator result. Which execution mode avoids re-queuing between iterations?

options.text: Job mode — submit each iteration as its own job, which usually reaches the QPU sooner than holding a session open.
Combine all iterations into a single primitive job
Batch mode — add each optimizer iteration to the batch as it is produced, since a batch typically keeps the QPU allocated to you between its jobs.
Job mode — each iteration as its own job, since Runtime typically raises a returning user's fair-share priority after the first job lands.

explanation.correct: A session gives dedicated, exclusive access to the QPU for a window, so an iterative workload whose next input depends on the previous result runs back-to-back without each job re-entering the fair-share queue. This is the documented use case for sessions: iterative workloads requiring frequent classical-quantum communication.

distractors.A: Batch mode is for independent jobs that are all available at the outset; here each iteration's parameters depend on the previous result, so the jobs cannot be submitted together and batching provides no benefit.
distractors.C: Submitting each iteration as a separate job sends every iteration back through the fair-share queue, so it does not reach the QPU sooner — each job waits its own turn, which is exactly what a session avoids.
distractors.D: The iterations cannot be one job: iteration n+1's parameters are computed classically from iteration n's result, so they are unknown when the job would be submitted.
distractors.E: A batch does not hold the QPU between jobs: batched jobs get no exclusive access, and other users' (and calibration) jobs may run in between. Batch also assumes the jobs are known at the outset, which is exactly what an optimizer-driven loop cannot provide.
distractors.F: Fair-share scheduling balances usage across users and projects; it does not accumulate priority for whoever submits most often. Every iteration would queue from scratch, which is exactly the round trip a session removes.
